1What You Will Learn

Note

Acronyms in this note. PII: personally identifiable information; ETL: extract, transform, load; EMR: Elastic MapReduce; LF: Lake Formation; KMS: Key Management Service; RDS: Relational Database Service; ECR: Elastic Container Registry; AMI: Amazon Machine Image; IAM: Identity and Access Management; SNS: Simple Notification Service; GDPR: General Data Protection Regulation; DMS: Database Migration Service; SQS: Simple Queue Service

  • Grant permissions for data sharing, for example Amazon Redshift data sharing
  • Identify PII with Amazon Macie together with AWS Lake Formation
  • Prevent backups and replication of data to disallowed Regions
  • View configuration changes with AWS Config
  • Maintain data sovereignty
  • Manage data access through Amazon SageMaker Catalog projects
  • Describe a data governance framework and data sharing patterns

2Granting Permissions for Data Sharing (skill 4.5.1)

Running case

Kestrel Freight Shares Data Safely

  • The analytics account wants the billing warehouse without copying it
  • A partner should see delivery statuses, but no customer names
  • A regulator limits where data may be stored
  • Your job: share the right data, to the right people, in the right places
Way to share How it works Remember
Amazon Redshift data sharing A producer cluster or Serverless workgroup creates a datashare (schemas, tables, views, functions); consumers (other clusters, workgroups, accounts, Regions) query it live with their own compute No copy, no ETL; data is current and transactionally consistent; consumers get read access; works with RA3 and Serverless; admins grant and authorize the share (and AWS Data Exchange can publish datashares to subscribers)
AWS Lake Formation cross-account sharing Grant database, table, column or row permissions to another account, an organization or its roles; recipients create resource links and query with Athena, Redshift Spectrum or EMR Fine-grained (columns, rows, LF-tags); permissions managed centrally; uses AWS RAM underneath
Amazon S3 sharing Bucket or access point policies, cross-account roles, S3 Replication, presigned URLs Coarser (object level); simplest for files; remember KMS key access (Module 16)
AWS Data Exchange Find, subscribe to and publish third-party datasets (to S3, Redshift and more) For external sharing and data products
Amazon SageMaker Catalog Publish assets and approve subscriptions between projects Business-driven sharing (section 7)
  • Share by view or column list, not the whole table, to hide sensitive columns
  • Principle of least privilege applies to sharing: named consumers, read-only, purpose-limited, time-boxed, logged (CloudTrail)
Exam tip

"Share live warehouse data with another account's Redshift without copying it" → Redshift data sharing (datashares). "Share lake tables with column and row limits" → Lake Formation cross-account grants.

3Identifying PII with Amazon Macie and Lake Formation (skill 4.5.2)

  • PII (personally identifiable information) is data that identifies a person: names, addresses, phone numbers, national IDs, financial and health data
  • Amazon Macie discovers and reports sensitive data in Amazon S3 using machine learning and pattern matching:
    • Managed data identifiers (names, addresses, credit card and bank numbers, national IDs, credentials) and custom data identifiers (your own regular expressions)
    • Automated sensitive data discovery (continuous sampling across your buckets) and sensitive data discovery jobs (scheduled or one-time, on chosen buckets)
    • Findings go to the console, Amazon EventBridge and AWS Security Hub; it also reports bucket inventory and policy problems (public, unencrypted, shared)
  • With AWS Lake Formation: use Macie's results to tag the affected tables and columns (for example an LF-tag sensitivity = pii) and then grant or deny access by tag, so only authorized roles see PII columns, and new tagged data is protected automatically (Module 15)
  • Other PII tools: the AWS Glue detect-PII transform (find and redact in a pipeline), Amazon Comprehend (PII in text), Redshift dynamic data masking and DataBrew masking (Module 16)
  • Process: discover → classify (tag) → restrict (permissions) → mask or minimize → monitor
Exam tip

"Find personal data in S3 buckets and restrict who can read it" → Amazon Macie for discovery, then Lake Formation tag-based access control.

4Preventing Backups and Replication to Disallowed Regions (skill 4.5.3)

  • Data stays in a Region unless you move it, but replication, cross-Region copies and global features can move it: S3 Replication, DynamoDB global tables, RDS and Redshift cross-Region snapshot copy, AWS Backup cross-Region copy, Aurora Global Database, ECR and AMI copies
  • Preventive controls:
    • Service control policies (SCPs) in AWS Organizations that deny actions when aws:RequestedRegion is not in the approved list (with exceptions for global services)
    • IAM policies and permissions boundaries with the same Region condition
    • S3: replication rules only to approved destination buckets; bucket policies and IAM that deny s3:ReplicateObject to other Regions
    • AWS Backup: backup plans and vault access policies that allow copies only to approved vaults and Regions
    • AWS Control Tower data residency guardrails and disabling unused Regions (opt-in Regions stay off)
    • KMS keys in the allowed Region (avoid multi-Region keys that replicate key material elsewhere)
  • Detective controls: AWS Config rules and conformance packs (for example S3 replication to unapproved Regions, unencrypted or public resources), CloudTrail alerts on replication, copy and global table actions
  • Test the guardrail: try an action in a blocked Region and confirm it is denied
Exam tip

"Make sure no one can replicate or back up data outside the EU" → an SCP that denies actions outside approved Regions, plus replication and backup rules that name only approved destinations.

5Viewing Configuration Changes with AWS Config (skill 4.5.4)

  • AWS Config records the configuration of AWS resources and how it changes over time (a configuration item per change, with relationships between resources)
  • Uses: a timeline of what changed and when for a bucket, security group, database or role; compliance against rules; troubleshooting and audits
  • Rules: managed rules (for example s3-bucket-public-read-prohibited, encrypted-volumes, rds-storage-encrypted) and custom rules (Lambda or Guard); evaluated on change or on a schedule; conformance packs bundle rules and remediation
  • Remediation: automatic or manual fixes through AWS Systems Manager Automation
  • Scope and delivery: aggregators collect multiple accounts and Regions; configuration snapshots and history are delivered to S3; notifications go to SNS and EventBridge; advanced queries use SQL across resources
  • Config vs CloudTrail: Config shows the state of a resource and its history; CloudTrail shows who made the API call: use both for an audit trail
Exam tip

"What was the configuration of the bucket policy last week, and is it compliant?" → AWS Config (timeline and rules). "Who changed it?" → CloudTrail.

6Data Sovereignty (skill 4.5.5)

  • Data residency = where data is stored; data sovereignty = the data is subject to the laws of the country where it is located (and who can compel access)
  • Why it matters: privacy and sector laws (for example GDPR, public-sector and health rules) may require data to stay in a country or region, limit transfers, and require local control of keys
  • How to maintain it on AWS:
    • Choose the Region that satisfies the law and create resources only there
    • Restrict Regions with SCPs and Control Tower guardrails; do not enable other Regions
    • Keep copies, backups, logs and analytics in-Region (cross-Region features off or limited; Section 4)
    • Control encryption keys: KMS keys in-Region, customer managed keys, optionally CloudHSM or external key store
    • Tag and classify data by residency requirement and enforce with LF-tags and Config rules
    • Document and audit where data lives and flows (lineage, Config, CloudTrail)
    • Check provider options for sovereign or isolated environments if the law requires them [Verify live]

7SageMaker Catalog Projects and Data Access (skill 4.5.6)Verify live

  • In Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio, data access is managed by project (Module 14): a project is the unit that publishes data and subscribes to data
  • Producer project: brings data in (for example Glue Data Catalog tables, Redshift tables, S3 data), adds business metadata (glossary terms, descriptions), and publishes assets to the catalog
  • Consumer project: searches the catalog, requests a subscription to an asset with a reason, and, once approved by the owner or steward, its members can query the data in their tools
  • Under the hood: grants are created for the project's role (through Lake Formation or Redshift sharing), so access is scoped to the project, can be revoked, and is audited
  • Governance benefits: business owners approve access, access follows the project and its members, everything is cataloged and logged
Exam tip

"Teams must request access to published datasets, owners approve, and access is limited to the requesting project" → SageMaker Catalog publish and subscribe with projects.

8Governance Frameworks and Data Sharing Patterns (skill 4.5.7)

Governance framework: what it contains

Part What it covers
Policies and standards Rules for data use, retention, sharing, naming
Roles Data owner (accountable), steward (maintains quality and definitions), custodian (technical operation), consumer
Classification Public, internal, confidential, restricted (PII, financial)
Catalog and metadata Technical and business catalogs, glossary (Module 7)
Quality Rules, monitoring, ownership (Module 13)
Security and privacy Authentication, authorization, encryption, masking, privacy law compliance (Modules 14–16)
Lifecycle Retention, archive, deletion (Module 8)
Lineage and audit Where data came from and who used it (Modules 9 and 17)
Metrics and compliance Measure adoption, quality, incidents; report

Data sharing patterns

Pattern Idea Fits when
Centralized One team and one lake own, store and serve the data Small organization, strong central team
Hub and spoke (cross-account sharing) A central account holds governed data and shares it to consumer accounts (Lake Formation, Redshift data sharing, RAM) Many consumers, central control
Data mesh Domains own and publish data products; central platform provides catalog, standards and federated governance Large organization, domain expertise, scale
External sharing AWS Data Exchange or controlled copies and APIs Partners and customers
Exam tip

A governance question is usually about who owns the data, how it is classified, who may use it, and how that is proven: choose the answer that assigns ownership, classifies, catalogs, restricts, and audits.

9Exam Q&A

9.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer; some ask for two)

S1Kestrel Freight's analytics account needs to query the billing warehouse in another account's Amazon Redshift without copying the data. Which feature fits?

  • ANightly UNLOAD and COPY
  • BRedshift data sharing
  • CAWS DMS full load
  • DS3 Glacier
Show the answer

Answer: B. A datashare lets consumers query live producer data with their own compute, with no copy or ETL.

S2A company must find personal data stored in many S3 buckets and then limit who can read the tagged columns in lake tables. Which combination fits?

  • AAWS Config alone, with rules that look for personal data in objects
  • BAmazon Macie for discovery and Lake Formation tag-based access control for restriction
  • CAmazon CloudFront signed URLs for the buckets that hold personal data
  • DAmazon Kinesis Data Streams with a consumer that scans each record
Show the answer

Answer: B. Macie discovers sensitive data in S3, and Lake Formation LF-tags grant or deny access by sensitivity.

S3A regulation requires that customer data and its backups never leave the EU. Which TWO controls help enforce this? (Select TWO.)

  • AAn SCP that denies actions when aws:RequestedRegion is not an approved EU Region
  • BDisable CloudTrail
  • CReplication and backup rules whose destinations are only approved EU Regions
  • DEnable S3 Transfer Acceleration
  • EUse multi-Region KMS keys in every Region
Show the answer

Answer: A, C. An SCP blocks use of other Regions, and replication and backup destinations restricted to approved Regions prevent copies leaving. Multi-Region keys and global acceleration move or expose more.

S4A security team needs to see how a security group and an S3 bucket policy changed over the last month and whether they comply with company rules. Which service provides the configuration timeline and compliance?

  • AAmazon Athena
  • BAWS Config
  • CAWS Glue
  • DAmazon SQS
Show the answer

Answer: B. AWS Config records resource configuration history and evaluates it against rules.

S5A large company wants each business domain to own and publish its own data products while a central team provides the catalog, standards and governance. Which pattern is this?

  • AData mesh
  • BA single centralized lake owned by one team
  • CA spreadsheet export process
  • DHub and spoke with no domain ownership
Show the answer

Answer: A. A data mesh has domain-owned data products with federated governance and a shared catalog.

10Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Redshift data sharing Live, no copy, producer/consumer, own compute, read access, cross-account and cross-Region, RA3/Serverless, publish via Data Exchange
Lake Formation sharing Cross-account grants to tables/columns/rows/LF-tags; RAM; resource links
Macie Discovers sensitive data in S3 (managed + custom identifiers, automated discovery, jobs); findings to EventBridge/Security Hub; pair with LF-tags
Region control SCP deny with aws:RequestedRegion, replication/backup destinations, Control Tower guardrails, in-Region KMS, Config rules
AWS Config Resource configuration history, rules (managed/custom), conformance packs, aggregators, remediation (Systems Manager); CloudTrail = who
Sovereignty Residency vs sovereignty; Region choice, SCPs, in-Region copies and keys, classification tags, documented flows
SageMaker Catalog Projects publish and subscribe; owner approves; project-scoped, revocable, audited access
Governance Policies, roles (owner, steward, custodian), classification, catalog, quality, security/privacy, lifecycle, lineage/audit; patterns: centralized, hub and spoke, data mesh, external (Data Exchange)
